angle: TRAP AVOIDANCE and the props/sharp-book rule layered on the universe the app already bets: rules that REMOVE the bets most likely to lose to the close (long lead, wide Novig book, falling edge, low edge, sharp veto bar, few books, long price) and rules that RAISE the bar where the evidence is thin (a higher edge floor for props with no sharp PASS), ranked by CLV gained per bet dropped, with the cost of each in bets and dollars a day at the auto-bet's caps.
tried_count_detail: 107 candidate drop rules/thresholds on the app's universe, by family: lead x11, sharp x10, prop_floor x11, ev_floor x5, check x13, books x15, price x6, looks x3, stat x9, league x2, liquidity x3, lister x2, combo x10, sharp_inc x4, spread x3; 95 were testable for the max-over-tries adjustment (>= 6 dropped and >= 20 kept closes). Each was also split by close source, and the final 8 were checked on 2-3 wider universes and three half definitions (those checks are not counted in tried_count).
baseline: The app's own universe U = shown by the CNO list & listed EV >= 2.5% & odds -200..+130 & props/moneylines/spreads & first listed within 24 h: 182 bets, 39 games, 80.7 a day, avg $354 available; CLV +1.37% [+0.07, +2.85] on 120 closes in 35 games, beat the close 64%; ROI -3.7% [-21.4, +12.9] on 174 settled bets in 38 games; vs Tracker closes +2.17% [+0.48, +4.00] on 56 closes in 27 games; vs independent closes +0.54% [-1.77, +2.53] on 38 closes in 19 games. Judged part UJ (book page read, the only bets the auto-bet can place): 75 bets, CLV +1.38% [-0.04, +3.07] on 64 closes in 25 games. Rules are measured as kept-minus-dropped CLV on the same universe, plus the same flag on the wider universes M, S, W (within 24 h).

rules.name: Wide Novig book: skip a judged bet whose two sides cost 2 cents or more over $1
rules.rationale: Novig's own book is thin or stale when the price of this side plus the price of the other side comes to 1.02 or more. Those bets lose to the consensus close more often than the rest (the traps analyst's second sign, re-checked here on the app's universe and on wider ones). It needs the other side's price, which is logged only with the book page (judged bets), so it applies to the bets the auto-bet can place. It is a LONG-LEAD sign: inside 6 h it adds nothing (wider judged universe WJ, within 6 h: +0.08 pts [-1.75, +1.48], 30 dropped), and 7 of its 17 dropped bets are the over-6 h ones the 6 h guard would also drop, so it is an alternative to the guard (or a belt-and-braces layer if the guard stays at 24 h), not an addition. Cost: drops 17 of 75 bets (23%; 7.5 a day), keeps 25.7 a day. Bets the auto-bet could still place (book page read, 3+ agree, not vetoed): 15.1 a day instead of 20.8, $72 a day at the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game) instead of $97, or $31 instead of $42 at its quarter-Kelly stake (never over $3.50); expected CLV worth about $1.61 a day instead of $1.11 at the caps ($0.69 vs $0.48 at quarter-Kelly). The whole list at the caps: $125 a day vs $159.
rules.verdict: Best CLV gain per bet dropped. Replicates on wider universes on all closes (WJ +2.15 pts [+0.90, +3.41], 80 dropped closes, 27 games) AND on independent closes (WJ +1.58 [+0.32, +2.94]), same sign in both game-start halves. Thin inside the app's universe (16 dropped closes, 11 games, interval touches 0) and not significant after the multiple-tries haircut.
rules.question_for_tj: QUESTION FOR TJ (it would only make the auto-bet stricter): skip a bet when Novig's price for this side plus the other side's price is 1.02 or more?  Pre-registered test on new games: about 25 games with closes in total (the app's universe has 25 so far) if the effect is as observed, about 101 if it is half.

The same flag on wider universes (single-rule one-sided wild-cluster p): MJ 0.059, SJ 0.013, WJ 0.003.

rules.name: 6 h trap guard (today 24 h) plus skip when the book page's own edge is 1 point or more under the list's edge
rules.rationale: Two decision-time signs layered: first listed within 6 h (the repo default; Tj's phone is at 24 h) and, for a bet whose book page was read, the page's own consensus EV (ab_checkEv) not more than 1 point under the EV the list showed (a falling edge between the list and the page). The falling-edge sign works only inside 6 h (WJ within 6 h +3.83 pts [+1.61, +5.49], 10 dropped closes; app universe within 6 h +5.75 [+3.68, +9.13], 5 dropped) and does nothing beyond 6 h; one of the falling-edge half's dropped closes is a -9.3% Tracker close (a bet Tj placed 35 minutes before the start); for the combined rule the worst dropped close is a -30.6% long-lead bet, and without it the gap is still +3.05 pts [+1.09, +5.13]. Cost: drops 36 of 75 bets (48%; 16.0 a day), keeps 17.3 a day. Bets the auto-bet could still place (book page read, 3+ agree, not vetoed): 13.3 a day instead of 20.8, $63 a day at the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game) instead of $97, or $27 instead of $42 at its quarter-Kelly stake (never over $3.50); expected CLV worth about $1.96 a day instead of $1.11 at the caps ($0.85 vs $0.48 at quarter-Kelly). The whole list at the caps: $82 a day vs $159.
rules.verdict: Largest kept CLV (+3.30%) and the clearest gap, same sign on every wider universe and both game-start halves; but (a) only 4 of its kept closes and 10 of its dropped closes are independent closes, and on independent closes the gain is +1.1 pts [-0.9, +3.4] in the app's universe and about 0 on the wider ones (WJ -0.04, 43 vs 52 closes); (b) it keeps only 39 of 75 judged bets; (c) the falling-edge half has only 5 dropped closes inside 6 h in the app's universe.

rules.name: Trap guard 6 h: only bets first listed within 6 h of the start (today 24 h)
rules.rationale: The only trap sign that is large on the wide samples: first-look lead over 6 h loses to the consensus close (wider universe W: kept +1.41% on 256 closes vs dropped -0.37% on 412, +1.79 pts [+0.93, +2.68], 69 games; within the same game +2.56 [+1.35, +3.81] over 28 games, 82% of games positive). It is the repo's own default (TrapGuard.DEFAULT_EARLY_HOURS = 6). Only 3 of the 106 dropped bets re-enter the 6 h window still listed and passing, so the first-look cut is what the guard really does here. Cost: drops 106 of 182 bets (58%; 47.0 a day), keeps 33.7 a day. Bets the auto-bet could still place (book page read, 3+ agree, not vetoed): 14.2 a day instead of 20.8, $67 a day at the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game) instead of $97, or $29 instead of $42 at its quarter-Kelly stake (never over $3.50); expected CLV worth about $1.90 a day instead of $1.11 at the caps ($0.81 vs $0.48 at quarter-Kelly). The whole list at the caps: $158 a day vs $346.
rules.verdict: Best supported by sample size and by the halves (both game-start halves positive: +2.45 and +1.75 pts). Inside the app's universe the interval touches 0 (+2.12 [-0.58, +5.23], 51 kept vs 69 dropped closes, 20 dropped games). The gap shows against Tracker closes (+3.15 in the app's universe, +2.85 in W) and ESPN (+2.11 in W) but NOT against Novig's own last trades (W -0.15 [-1.7, +1.2]); on all independent closes W +0.89 [-0.11, +1.97]. rules.name: Props with no sharp-book PASS need a 3.5% edge (a higher floor where the evidence is thin)
rules.rationale: Tj's 2026-10-03 alternative to requiring a sharp book: keep every prop the sharp book PASSED at the app's 2.5%, but ask 3.5% of a prop with no sharp verdict (NO_SHARP, or no book page read). It is the same thing as the general edge floor in the data: at the same low EV (under 3.5%) a PASS adds only about +1 pt (U +1.07 [-1.77, +4.36], S +1.06 [-0.51, +2.49], W +0.98 [-0.35, +2.06]; 0 on independent closes), while at 3.5% or more a prop with no PASS beats the close as much as a PASSED one (S not-PASSED +3.50 [+0.34, +6.36] vs PASSED +2.43 [+0.09, +4.80]). Cost: drops 57 of 182 bets (31%; 25.3 a day), keeps 55.4 a day. Bets the auto-bet could still place (book page read, 3+ agree, not vetoed): 20.4 a day instead of 20.8, $95 a day at the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game) instead of $97, or $41 instead of $42 at its quarter-Kelly stake (never over $3.50); expected CLV worth about $1.09 a day instead of $1.11 at the caps ($0.47 vs $0.48 at quarter-Kelly). The whole list at the caps: $237 a day vs $346.
rules.verdict: Cannot be tested on its intended group: only 7 props in the app's universe are judged NO_SHARP (3 closes). The nearest test (not PASSED, edge under 3.5%) gives +2.06 pts [-0.31, +4.80] (30 dropped closes, 14 games), not better than the general 3.5% floor (+1.96), and its sign flips between game-start halves (+3.57, -0.76). Wider universes agree in sign (W +1.51 [+0.59, +2.28]).

Pre-registered test on new games: about 54 games with closes in total (the app's universe has 35 so far) if the effect is as observed, about 216 if it is half.

rules.name: Raise the sharp veto bar from 1% to 2% (skip when the sharpest book's own edge is 1-2%)
rules.rationale: Today the auto-bet skips a bet only when the sharpest book that prices both sides gives Novig's price under 1% (the veto). Tested on what that veto lets through: the extra bets a 2% bar would drop (sharp edge 1-2%), and the 3% and 4% bars in the screen table. Cost: drops 7 of 58 bets (12%; 3.1 a day), keeps 22.6 a day. Bets the auto-bet could still place (book page read, 3+ agree, not vetoed): 18.2 a day instead of 20.8, $86 a day at the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game) instead of $97, or $37 instead of $42 at its quarter-Kelly stake (never over $3.50); expected CLV worth about $0.91 a day instead of $1.11 at the caps ($0.39 vs $0.48 at quarter-Kelly). The whole list at the caps: $108 a day vs $121.
rules.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED: the dropped bets beat the close as much as the kept ones (+0.22 pts [-2.90, +4.55]; 6 dropped closes; wider SA +0.23, WA +0.18, both intervals straddle 0) and the sign flips between halves. The veto at 1% itself: in the app's universe it drops 13 closes with CLV +1.37% vs kept +1.39% (diff +0.01 [-2.05, +2.33]); in all props VETOED props closed -0.10% (63 bets, 44 closes) vs PASSED +0.78% (178 bets, 139 closes), a gap of +0.88 pts [-1.05, +2.53] (props analyst) that is not distinguishable from 0 and vanishes inside the app's universe. It neither costs nor saves measurable edge.
rules.question_for_tj: No change proposed. Leave the veto at 1%; a bar above it buys no CLV in 2.3 days of data.

rules.name: Props must have a sharp-book PASS (Tj's 2026-10-03 question)
rules.rationale: Requiring a PASS from a sharp-ranked book (Kalshi, ProphetX, FanDuel, Caesars, DraftKings) before a prop is listed or bet. In the app's universe this keeps 56 of 182 bets (the 51 PASSED props plus 5 non-props), because 102 props have no book page read (a prop with no page cannot pass) and 7 are NO_SHARP. Cost: drops 126 of 182 bets (69%; 55.8 a day), keeps 24.8 a day. Bets the auto-bet could still place (book page read, 3+ agree, not vetoed): 19.9 a day instead of 20.8, $93 a day at the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game) instead of $97, or $40 instead of $42 at its quarter-Kelly stake (never over $3.50); expected CLV worth about $1.09 a day instead of $1.11 at the caps ($0.46 vs $0.48 at quarter-Kelly). The whole list at the caps: $117 a day vs $346.
rules.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED: kept CLV +1.32% vs dropped +1.40% (diff -0.08 pts [-2.66, +2.71]); the dropped group includes the best props in the log (not-PASSED props at 3.5% or more: +2.61% in the app's universe, +3.50% in S, +3.34% in W). Reproduces the app's own what-if (all props: PASSED 178 bets +0.78% on 139 closes, VETOED 63 bets -0.10% on 44 closes, exchange-only 141 bets +0.27%). Which book: re-checked, PASS by an originating book (FanDuel/Caesars/DraftKings) is the only kind that beat the close (all props: 37 bets +2.55% [+1.34, +3.93] on 31 closes, 21 games; in the app's universe 15 bets +5.17% [+4.04, +6.40], 14 games) while PASS by an exchange (Kalshi/ProphetX) did not (all props 141 bets +0.27% [-1.03, +1.23]; app's universe 36 bets -0.45% [-2.55, +1.63]); but only 4 of the originating-book closes are independent closes (+0.49), so it is the consensus re-read speaking, and it keeps only 8% of the bets (15 of 182, about 7 a day).

props_sharp_question.answer: Requiring a sharp PASS for props does not raise CLV enough to pay for the bets it drops: in the app's universe it keeps 56 of 182 bets and the kept CLV is +1.32% vs +1.40% dropped (diff -0.08 pts [-2.66, +2.71]); in all props PASSED +0.78% (139 closes) vs VETOED -0.10% (44) is +0.88 pts [-1.05, +2.53], and by game start it flips. Which book matters: PASS by an originating book (FanDuel/Caesars/DraftKings) beat the close (all props 37 bets +2.55%; app's universe 15 bets +5.17%) and PASS by an exchange (Kalshi/ProphetX) did not (141 bets +0.27%; app's universe 36 bets -0.45%), but nearly all those closes are Tracker closes (independent closes: originating 4, exchange 31 in all props). A higher edge for props with no sharp book cannot be tested on its own group (7 judged NO_SHARP props, 3 closes, in the app's universe); the edge effect is the same with or without a PASS: props at 3.5% or more beat the close by +2.6 to +3.5 pts whether or not a sharp book passed them, and at the same low edge a PASS adds only about +1 pt (intervals include 0, 0 on independent closes). A 3.5% edge for props with no PASS is therefore the same as the general 3.5% floor in this data. Cost of each choice in bets a day is in rules 4, 6 and 8 (rule 8 drops 55.8 of 80.7 bets a day).

notes:
READ THIS FIRST.
1) POWER. The app's own universe U (shown by the CNO list, edge >= 2.5%, odds -200..+130, props/moneylines/spreads, first listed within 24 h) is 182 bets in 39 games (80.7 a day, 177 of them props, 143 NFL); only 120 have a close, in 35 games, and 100 of those closes are games of ONE day (Oct 4, a single NFL Sunday slate), so every 'half' is a half of one slate. Its CLV is +1.37% [+0.07, +2.85] on 120 closes in 35 games; against the Tracker's CNO re-read (+2.17% [+0.48, +4.00] on 56 closes in 27 games) and against independent closes (ESPN, Pinnacle, Novig last trades of 3+; +0.54% [-1.77, +2.53] on 38 closes in 19 games). The bets the auto-bet can actually place (book page read, not vetoed, 3+ agreeing, 2+ two-sided) are 47 bets in 21 games (20.8 a day), 45 closes, CLV +1.14%, only 4 independent closes.
2) LUCK. 107 candidate drop rules/thresholds were tried on the app's universe (95 with >= 6 dropped and >= 20 kept closes enter the max test; about four times as many evaluations if the wider-universe, close-source and half checks are counted). Nothing inside the app's universe survives that count: the best adjusted p is 0.16 (permutation within game-day) / 0.29-0.38 (wild-cluster bootstrap, game as cluster), and among 95 rules with no real effect the best one would show p of about 0.01 by chance. The single-rule p-values in each rule are what the rule would earn without counting the tries. The bet-level permutation ignores same-game correlation (anti-conservative for game-level flags such as lead time), so the cluster bootstrap is the number to trust.
3) WHAT REPLICATES. Only on wider universes whose bets the app would not all take (M: shown, within 24 h, edge >= 2.5%, any kind or odds, 138 closes; S: all shown within 24 h, 378 closes; W: all bets within 24 h, 668 closes in 69 games). There the sign holds for: first listed over 6 h out (W +1.79 pts [+0.93, +2.68], within the same game +2.56 [+1.35, +3.81] over 28 games, 82% positive), a wide Novig book (WJ +2.15 [+0.90, +3.41]; on independent closes +1.58 [+0.32, +2.94]), the 3.5% edge floor (W +3.24 [+1.05, +5.27]) and a falling edge inside 6 h (WJ +3.83 [+1.61, +5.49], 10 dropped closes). These confirm the SIGN of an effect, not its size inside the app's universe.
4) WHICH CLOSE. Almost every effect shows against consensus-type closes (the Tracker's CNO re-read, ESPN/DraftKings) and little against Novig's own last trades or all independent closes: the 6 h guard gap is +2.85 on Tracker closes and +2.11 on ESPN but -0.15 [-1.7, +1.2] on Novig trades of 3+ in W (all independent closes in W: +0.89 [-0.11, +1.97]). Tj's trap story (sharps moving Novig's price) predicts the Novig-trades yardstick; the app's EV model (consensus vs Novig) predicts the consensus yardstick. Both are reported for every rule.
5) NOT SUPPORTED (numbers in the screen table): raising the sharp veto bar (1% -> 2%: +0.22 [-2.90, +4.55]; 3% and 4% bars also null); requiring a sharp PASS (-0.08 [-2.66, +2.71]); few books behind the fair (in the app's universe 5 or fewer books closed BETTER: +5.30% vs +0.76%, i.e. the opposite of a trap sign; in W the sign is weak); a long price (american >= +110: dropped group +2.28% vs kept +0.29%, opposite sign; heavy favourites cost >= .55 are a trap in W, +1.41 [+0.18, +2.22], but only 8 bets in the app's universe); few agreeing books (<= 3 agreeing: dropped CLV +2.52% vs kept +0.83%, opposite sign); book dissent (agreeShare < 1: +1.78 [-0.40, +4.04] in the app's universe, 0 on shown and wider universes); low liquidity (bets with under $50 available closed better: +3.12% vs +0.24%); falling EV between the first look and the page read (7 closes, +3.36 [-3.81, +10.74]); prop stats (Receptions -3.82% on 7 closes in 6 games; Shots On Goal +4.72% on 10; Rushing Attempts +7.23% on 7; one NFL slate each).
6) TJ'S PROPS QUESTION: see props_sharp_question. Short answer: do not require a sharp prop book; a higher edge for props with no sharp PASS is the same as a general 3.5% floor in this data and cannot be tested on its own group (7 judged NO_SHARP props).
7) DOLLARS. At the caps ($5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game; the live setting is a quarter-Kelly stake never over $3.50) the whole list is about $346 a day and the bets the auto-bet can place are about $97 a day (20.8 bets a day); at its quarter-Kelly stake about $42 a day. Even if every CLV figure here were true, the expected CLV value of those bets is about $1.1 a day at the caps ($0.5 at quarter-Kelly), so each rule moves expected dollars by cents to about a dollar a day; a rule that drops bets with CLV above 0 (the 6 h guard drops +0.46% bets in the app's universe) costs expected value unless the dropped bets are truly negative, and its gain is in CLV per dollar and fewer orders, not in dollars. The daily cap ($500) does not bind in the app's universe ($346 a day at the caps).
8) OVERLAP. Rules 1, 3 and 5 are mostly one thing (long lead): the wide-book sign works only beyond 6 h and the falling-edge sign only inside 6 h, so '6 h guard + falling edge' (rule 2) is the layered version; a rule that drops over-6 h bets already drops 7 of the wide-book rule's 17 bets.
9) DATA TRAPS. (a) sharpVerdict is NO_SHARP by default for 1442 bets with no page read: use ab_verdict.notna() for 'judged'. (b) The page is read a median 18.5 min (mean 154) after the first look, so a rule using page fields needs the page and is evaluated at the first-look price, not the price at the page read. (c) 1-2-trade Novig closes are prices, not closes: every rule also has close_ok numbers (clv_close_ok). (d) The phone's trap guard is at 24 h (diagnostics: 'only on games starting within 24 h'); the repo default (TrapGuard.DEFAULT_EARLY_HOURS) is 6 h. (e) All CLV is at the first-listed price, 63% of bets never change price while listed; the first-look rules do not use look-ahead (lead, EV, books, page fields only).
10) LOG NEXT TIME: a book page for every bet in the app's universe (so every prop has a verdict and the other side's price at first look); Novig's own last-trade close for every started bet (824 started bets have no Novig outcome id); an independent close for props; the price and EV at the moment the auto-bet would have bet; at least 5 game days so 'halves' are different slates.
EVERY RULE IS A QUESTION FOR TJ: all proposals only make the auto-bet stricter; none loosens a limit. Rules are ranked by CLV gained per bet dropped (clv_gain_pts_per_10pct_of_bets_dropped) among rules whose gap keeps its sign in both game-start halves; rules that flip between halves (12 h guard, props floor) and null rules follow.

method.per_day_definition: bets / 2.256 days (study span from first to last first-look)
method.clv: closeFair/cost - 1 at the first-listed price (loader); close_ok drops Novig-trades closes of under 3 trades; independent closes = ESPN, Pinnacle, Novig last trades of 3+; Tracker closes = the CNO re-read for bets Tj placed
method.ci: game-clustered bootstrap (resample games, 1500-3000 draws) for kept and dropped CLV, ROI and the kept-minus-dropped gap
method.luck_single: one-sided P(kept-minus-dropped gap this large) under (a) a wild cluster bootstrap with Rademacher weights per game (6000 draws; null: the flag has no effect, games are the clusters) using the cluster-robust z, and (b) a permutation of CLV within game-day (start day) strata, 6000 draws, Welch z (bet-level, ignores same-game correlation)
method.luck_adjusted: the same statistics, taking the maximum z over the 95 testable rules in each null draw (Westfall-Young style single-step max-t); adjusted p = share of draws whose maximum is at least the observed z
method.halves: first_half/second_half = kept CLV for games starting before/after the median game start among the baseline's closes (balanced by closes); halves detail also gives first-look halves and the loader's firstDay cut (Oct 3-4 vs Oct 5-6: only 14 closes in the second half of the app's universe)
method.dollars: stake = min($5, Novig $ available at the price) for 'caps'; min($3.50, quarter-Kelly of the bet's own record, available) for 'kelly'; bets taken in first-look order, a game capped at $70 and an Eastern first-look day at $500; expected CLV $ = staked $ x mean CLV of the kept bets with closes (selection caveat: closes are a biased 33% of bets); autobet_eligible = book page read, not vetoed, 3+ agreeing, 2+ two-sided
method.expr_note: expr = bets the rule KEEPS (universe & ~drop_expr); every expr is a boolean pandas expression over df = load() alone (no derived columns) and reproduces the bet counts; universe_expr is the baseline set
method.gain_metric: clv_gain_pts_per_10pct_of_bets_dropped = (kept CLV - baseline CLV) / (share of bets dropped x 10)
